text:
alice: heads-up: after the 0a1b2c merge we're seeing a ~2.3x p95 spike on short-sequence decode paths in canary. not universal but reproducible on a subset of hosts

bob: I noticed higher tail on small-batch traffic too. looks like shortseq latency up starts ~30s after deploy. perf CI also flagged a +22% p95 on decode benchmark.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: commit 0a1b2c (fused-prefetch + kernel-selector heuristics) -> canary pool 3/5 hosts :rocket: 

carol: attaching a small perf sample from a repro run:
```
# top hotspots (sampled)
0x7f2a decode_kernel_choice  32%
0x7f1b fused_attention_prefetch 18%
0x6c9e kv_cache_lookup 14%
0x5a2d matmul_dispatch 8%
```
notably, kv_cache_lookup jumps from ~3% to ~14% on canary.

alice: interesting — my traces show kernel-selector routing more requests to the fused path for seq_len <= 16. previous default favored tiny-matmul path. seems heuristics changed thresholds.

dave: repro script I ran: `./bench_shortseq --batch=2 --seq=8 --iters=500` shows p95 18ms pre-merge -> 42ms post-merge on the same image. stack traces point at fused_attention_prefetch and increased memcpy around kv handling.

erin: I ran a quick bisect on the fused-prefetch commit series. disabling the new prefetch schedule (flip a flag) restores p95 to ~19ms. so it's likely the interaction between prefetch and KV cache warmup.

bob: can we get perf counters? I suspect extra memcpy / cache thrash during KV warmup causing the stall. maybe the prefetch path issues overlapping async copies for tiny batches.

carol: added a microprofile trace from a single request with seq=8 (shortened):
```
[0.0s] request recv
[0.6ms] kernel selection -> fused-prefetch path
[1.1ms] prefetch kickoff (async memcpy)
[1.9ms] kv cache lookup (miss) -> fetch remote KV
[5.0ms] wait on memcpy completion
[12.3ms] attention fused kernel start
```
Seems we now do prefetch + remote KV fetch concurrently, but memcpy completion blocks the fuse path longer than before.

alice: summary: heuristics now eagerly route shortseq to fused-prefetch which triggers different memory access pattern; on hosts with slightly noisier PCIe latency this amplifies tail.

dave: perf CI bisect: toggling `kernel_selector.shortseq_threshold` back to previous value fixes the CI benchmark.

erin: propose immediate mitigation: revert the selector change in canary (or set flag to old threshold) and open a follow-up to redesign prefetch interplay with kv cache.

bob: agree. revert on canary and hold rollout. also add a quick test in CI that simulates small-batch shortseq workload with KV miss to catch this.

carol: created a reproduce job: `repro/shortseq-kv-warmup` on infra, job id 4721. capturing traces and perf counters.

alice: assigned to dave to flip the flag in canary and coordinate revert if needed. dave can you patch?

dave: will patch the selector flag in canary now and roll back the fused-prefetch heuristic in the next hour. posting results shortly.

deploy-bot: rollback started for commit 0a1b2c -> rolling canary to previous image (3/5 hosts)

dave: rolled back selector to previous threshold on canary. early measurements: p95 back to ~20ms on repro job. leaving canary paused.

erin: next actions: (1) add CI regression for shortseq+kv-miss (2) rework prefetch to avoid blocking path when KV miss observed (3) add per-host PCIe latency gating to heuristics

alice: good. file a postmortem if rollout reached prod (it didn't). label as rollout-blocker/regression. thanks all. :thumbsup:
